relations.statement: Two data d1,d2 collapse iff for every well-formed context C, the plugging of d1 into C derives alike to the plugging of d2 into C.
relations.hypotheses: Well-formedness of contexts and the derivation-alike relation must be fixed; neither is declared in the source.

relations.statement: Two data d1,d2 are separable iff some well-formed context C exists whose pluggings of d1 and d2 do not derive alike; this is the negation of R-collapse.

lemmas.statement: For any two data, exactly one of collapse and separability holds.
lemmas.lean_skeleton:
theorem dichotomy {D C : Type} (plug : C → D → Prop) (a b : D) : (∀ c, plug c a ↔ plug c b) ∨ (∃ c, ¬ (plug c a ↔ plug c b)) := by
  by_cases h : ∀ c, (plug c a ↔ plug c b)
  · exact Or.inl h
  · exact Or.inr (by push_neg at h; exact h)

near_misses.claim: A finite census over rung three's rectangle decides collapse for all contexts.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: A census decides only the rows it enumerates; the target requires a procedure quantifying over every well-formed context, which the census does not give.

open_obligations: No generators grounded: no existing declarations were listed in the source.
Define the colours: data, context and derivation-alike.
Define the well-formedness of contexts and the plugging operation.
Build the decision procedure itself (X-1); no decision procedure is proposed.
Prove that the class count of observational classes (T-1, SD-C-2) is a finite computation in Lean.
Proofs of Y-2 (necessity of uniformity) and of deciding holding two or exhaustion at a regime remain pending.
The dichotomy skeleton is unelaborated and not marked proved.
